story_description: Users designing hooks in the Blaze Hooks Builder need to export their configurations to the correct provider-specific config paths so that the target CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or Codex CLI) can load and execute the hooks during agentic sessions.
task_description: Implement the HooksInstallationService that exports hook configurations to the correct provider-specific paths: Claude to .claude/settings.json, Gemini to .gemini/settings.json, and Codex to .codex/config.toml (TOML format). Handle path resolution, format conversion, file merging with existing configs, and atomic write operations.
atom_description: A Swift actor service (HooksInstallationService) that takes a HookConfiguration from the Hooks Builder, determines the target provider, resolves the correct config directory path relative to the project root, converts the hook data to the provider's native format (JSON for Claude/Gemini, TOML for Codex), merges with any existing configuration without overwriting unrelated settings, writes atomically using temporary file plus rename, and reports success or failure with detailed error messages.
problem_statement: The Blaze Hooks Builder creates hook configurations in a normalized internal format, but each CLI vendor expects hooks in different locations and potentially different formats. Without provider-specific export logic, users would have to manually create config directories, convert formats, and merge hook entries by hand, defeating the purpose of the visual builder. Additionally, careless writes could overwrite existing user configurations or leave partial files on error.
scope_in: Determine target config directory based on HookProvider enum (claude -> .claude/, gemini -> .gemini/, codex -> .codex/)
Resolve config directory path relative to project root URL from SessionStore or user selection
Create config directory if it does not exist (mkdir -p equivalent)
Convert HookConfiguration to provider-native JSON structure for Claude Code settings.json
Convert HookConfiguration to provider-native JSON structure for Gemini CLI settings.json
Convert HookConfiguration to TOML format for Codex CLI config.toml
Load existing config file if present to preserve non-hook settings (permissions, model preferences, etc.)
Deep merge hook entries with existing hooks section, replacing entries with matching descriptions or event+matcher combos
Write to temporary file first, then atomic rename to final path for crash safety
Return ExportResult with success/failure, path written, and any warnings about merged entries
Emit telemetry events for export attempts, successes, and failures
Handle Codex special case where hooks are limited to notify events only
scope_out: Actually executing hooks - that is HookRunner's responsibility in separate atom
Validating hook command syntax or testing if commands exist on PATH
Managing hook lifecycle (enable/disable) - handled by MultiProviderHooksService
Worktree-specific overrides - separate atom H009-CONTEXT handles worktree scope
UI for export action - ProviderSelectorView and ExportButton are separate atoms
Hook migration between providers - H007-MIGRATE handles conversion logic
Reading hooks back from exported files - MultiProviderHooksService handles loading
assumptions: Project root path is available from SessionStore.activeSession.projectPath or user-selected directory
HookConfiguration struct is already defined with provider, events, and hook entries
Provider-specific JSON schema follows each CLI's documented settings format
TOML serialization library (TOMLKit or equivalent) is available via SPM dependency
File system permissions allow writing to project subdirectories
Codex CLI will support a config.toml format for notify hooks at MVP time
constraints: Must not corrupt or lose existing config file contents on any error path
Must complete export operation within 500ms for reasonable UX responsiveness
Must handle concurrent export requests safely using actor isolation
Must preserve exact JSON formatting preferences if existing file has custom indentation
Must not export hooks to Codex if provider does not actually support hooks (show warning instead)
Must work with project paths containing spaces or unicode characters
Exported files must be valid and parseable by target CLI immediately after write
functional_requirements: FR1: Accept HookConfiguration with provider (HookProvider), hooks ([HookEntry]), and projectPath (URL) as input
FR3: Create config directory with FileManager.createDirectory(withIntermediateDirectories: true) if missing
FR4: Determine config filename from provider: settings.json for Claude/Gemini, config.toml for Codex
FR5: Load existing config file if present using JSONDecoder or TOMLDecoder respectively
FR6: Deep merge incoming hooks into existing config, preserving all non-hooks keys unchanged
FR7: For Claude/Gemini JSON, merge hook entries by event type key, then by description or matcher signature
FR8: For Codex TOML, convert hook entries to TOML table format with [hooks.EventName] sections
FR9: Serialize merged config using JSONEncoder with .prettyPrinted and .sortedKeys options for JSON
FR10: Serialize merged config using TOMLEncoder with standard formatting for TOML
FR11: Write serialized data to temporary file in same directory with .tmp extension
FR12: Atomic rename temporary file to final config filename using FileManager.moveItem
FR13: Delete temporary file on any error to avoid leaving orphaned files
FR14: Return ExportResult struct with status (success/failure), outputPath, warnings, and optional error
FR15: For Codex provider, check if hooks array contains non-notify hooks and add warning to result
FR16: Emit telemetry event hooks.export.started with provider and hook count on entry
FR17: Emit telemetry event hooks.export.completed with provider, success boolean, and duration on exit
FR18: Log detailed debug messages for each step to aid troubleshooting
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Export operation completes within 500ms for configs up to 50 hooks
NFR2: Service is thread-safe using Swift actor isolation pattern
NFR3: Memory usage stays under 10MB even for large existing config files
NFR4: File operations use atomic writes to prevent data loss on crash or power failure
NFR5: Error messages are human-readable and include suggested remediation steps
NFR6: Service is testable with mock file system for unit tests
NFR7: Supports project paths up to 4096 characters with any valid UTF-8 characters

edge_cases: Project path is nil or empty - return failure with clear error message asking user to select project
Config directory exists but is a file not directory - return failure suggesting manual removal
Existing config file is not valid JSON/TOML - preserve original as .backup, write new file, warn user
Existing config file is read-only - return failure with suggestion to check permissions
Disk is full during write - cleanup temp file, return failure with disk space warning
Two concurrent exports to same path - actor serializes them, second waits for first
Hooks array is empty - export valid config with empty hooks section, warn user
Provider is Codex but all hooks are non-notify events - return partialSuccess with all-skipped warning
Project path contains special characters (spaces, unicode) - URL encoding handles correctly
Config directory path exceeds PATH_MAX - return failure before attempting operations
failure_modes: FileManager.createDirectory throws - return failure with permission or path error details
JSONDecoder fails on existing config - backup original, proceed with fresh config, add warning
TOMLDecoder fails on existing config - backup original, proceed with fresh config, add warning
JSONEncoder throws during serialization - log internal error, return failure
Data.write(to:) throws during temp file write - cleanup any partial file, return failure
FileManager.moveItem throws during rename - delete temp file, return failure with specific error
FileManager.removeItem throws during cleanup - log warning but do not fail the export
Network drive disconnects mid-write - temp file orphaned, return failure
App terminates during write - temp file may remain, no corruption of original config
Sandboxed app lacks permission to project directory - return failure with permission request instructions
rollback_plan: If export corrupts or overwrites important config data: 1) Check for .backup file created before merge and restore it, 2) Use git checkout to restore original config if project is under version control, 3) Delete the problematic config file and let CLI regenerate defaults on next run, 4) Manually reconstruct from Blaze Hooks Builder which preserves the canonical state. The atomic write pattern means corruption should not occur - either the old file is intact or the new complete file replaces it.

risks: Atomic write may fail on network drives or removable media with different filesystem semantics
TOML serialization library may have bugs or produce non-standard output that Codex cannot parse
Concurrent writes from multiple Blaze instances could create race condition despite actor isolation
Deep merge logic may incorrectly match hooks leading to unintended overwrites
Existing config may use non-standard JSON features (comments, trailing commas) causing parse failure
mitigations: Detect filesystem type and warn user if atomic rename may not be supported; offer non-atomic fallback with confirmation
Add integration test that verifies exported TOML parses correctly with reference TOML parser; pin library version
Use file locking (flock) as additional protection beyond actor isolation; warn if lock cannot be acquired
Match hooks using composite key of event type plus description plus matcher JSON; never match on partial data
Use lenient JSON parsing for reading existing configs; strip comments and normalize before merge
risk_register.blast_radius: Affects only hook configuration files in .claude/, .gemini/, .codex/ directories. Does not modify project source code, session data, or app state. Worst case is one provider's config is corrupted requiring manual restoration.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If HooksInstallationService causes config corruption: 1) Restore from .backup file if created, 2) Use git to restore config files, 3) Delete corrupted config and let CLI regenerate, 4) Export hooks to a temp location and manually copy the hooks section into config file.
